summary: Of the eight Phase-1 findings put up for falsification, only three were touched by surviving evidence: finding #3 (T+2 vs an RBI T+1 mandate) is FALSIFIED — the operative RBI (Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025 prescribe no settlement day-count at all and expressly repeal the 2020 circular that carried Ts+1/Tp+1, replacing it with a contractual fairness-and-transparency test; finding #8 (Agent Studio roster) is CONFIRMED but must be corrected to "eight cards / seven distinct functions, of which Razorpay describes only four as production-ready, with Abandoned Cart built by SuperU and Nugget-by-Zomato and Subscription Recovery voice-powered by ElevenLabs"; finding #6 (Vulcan numbers are unaudited vendor marketing) is CONFIRMED by adversarial trade press that asked Razorpay for baseline, sample size and timeframe and received none as of 18 Aug 2026. On JOB 2, the verification round produced exactly two usable magnitudes — Baymard's global 70.22% cart-abandonment average with a confirmed ABSENCE of any India-specific or mobile/desktop-split benchmark, and TransUnion's India suspected-digital-fraud figures (7.1% economy-wide, but 2.5% retail and 1.2% at the financial-transaction stage) — and both are framed primarily as warnings against misuse rather than as clean problem sizings. Every other requested magnitude (RTO rate and cost per RTO, refund failure rate, SME DSO / MSME Samadhaan, reconciliation FTE-hours, involuntary churn from failed mandates) and every remaining Phase-1 finding (UPI AutoPay 20M monthly revocations, SBI ~30% approval, 92-96% blended success, fund holds/freezes, refunds as top complaint, DRHP confidentiality) failed to survive adversarial voting and must be carried forward as UNVERIFIED, not as established. None of the six high-value source types requested — Razorpay engineering blog, Razorpay research reports, 2026 leadership interviews, RazorpayX product pages, developer documentation, 2026 newsroom — yielded a claim that survived verification; the sole Razorpay-official source that did was the Agent Studio launch blog.

findings.claim: FALSIFIED — Phase-1 finding #3 is wrong: there is no RBI T+1 settlement mandate for payment aggregators in 2026, so Razorpay's T+2 standard settlement is not a regulation-vs-practice gap. The RBI (Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025 delegate settlement day-counts entirely to the PA-merchant contract, subject only to fairness and transparent disclosure, and affirmatively repeal the 2020 circular that carried the Ts+1/Tp+1 timelines.
findings.evidence: problem: Phase-1 asserted a compliance breach (T+2 practice vs T+1 mandate) that does not exist in the operative regulator text. | evidence: RBI Master Direction RBI/DPSS/2025-26/141, CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S-633/02-14-008/2025-26, dated 15 Sep 2025, effective immediately, applying to all bank and non-bank PAs. Chapter V Table 1: 'Credit to merchant's a/c: As per the agreement between the PA and the merchant. Such an agreement should be fair, equitable and must transparently mention the settlement timelines.' Also 'These Directions shall be effective immediately unless indicated otherwise for any specific provision herein.' Source type: regulator (primary). A verifier extracted the full 44,787-character PDF and ran regex over it: ZERO matches for 'T+1', 'Ts+1', 'Td+1', '+1 day', 'one working day', or even 'working day'; all 19 occurrences of 'settl*' inspected individually, none imposes a day-count. Annexure-3 item 1 repeals DPSS.CO.PD.No.1810/02.14.008/2019-20 dated 17 Mar 2020 — precisely the circular that carried Ts+1/Tp+1 — and para 21 states 'Save as provided herein, circulars listed in Annexure-3 stands repealed'. Corroborated by four independent legal analyses (Khaitan & Co ERGO 3 Oct 2025; Vinod Kothari Consultants Sep 2025; AZB Partners; IndiaCorpLaw 9 Oct 2025; The Digital Fifth), which describe 'the earlier T+1 and Td+1 structure' as 'replaced with commercially negotiated terms'. Counter-evidence found (enterslice.com, billcut.com asserting a T+1 obligation) is stale SEO content recycling the repealed 2020 guidelines and cites no paragraph of the 2025 MD. Staged provisions confirmed independently (due diligence in force 1 Jan 2026; wind-up for non-compliant entities 28 Feb 2026), consistent with the 'unless indicated otherwise' carve-out. No amendment or replacement instrument found as of 24 Aug 2026. | business_impact: NO MAGNITUDE FOUND (and none applicable — the finding is the removal of an asserted magnitude). | who_suffers: merchants, but only via a disclosure/fairness argument, not a compliance breach. | current_razorpay_solution: n/a. | remaining_gap: the residual, much weaker question is whether Razorpay's merchant agreement discloses its settlement timeline 'fairly, equitably and transparently'; separate NPCI/scheme and nodal-account rules were NOT examined and could still carry timing obligations. Note also that the corroborating claim built on Razorpay's own docs page (razorpay.com/docs/payments/settlements/ stating T+2) FAILED verification 0-3, so even the T+2 baseline is not independently confirmed here. | verdict: NOT A REAL PROBLEM as framed — Phase-1 finding #3 should be struck or rewritten as a transparency question.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED WITH CORRECTIONS — Phase-1 finding #8 stands on its roster and its coverage gaps, but three amendments are required: the launch page shows eight cards covering seven distinct functions (Abandoned Cart Conversion appears twice); Razorpay itself describes only FOUR agents as production-ready at launch, not seven; and at least two agents are partner-built rather than Razorpay-built.
findings.evidence: problem: Razorpay's agentic product surface does not cover several of the merchant pain points Phase 1 identified. | evidence: Razorpay-official launch blog, 12 Mar 2026 (retrieved 24 Aug 2026), lists exactly eight cards: Dispute Responder ('Auto-responds to chargebacks with optimized evidence'); Subscription Recovery ('Analyzes failed subscription payments with retry logic'); 'Abandoned Cart Conversion (Powered by SuperU)'; 'Abandoned Cart Conversion (Powered by Nugget by Zomato)'; Cashflow Forecaster ('Predicts cash position 3-7 days ahead'); RTO Shield ('Detects high-risk COD orders before dispatch'); RTO Insights ('Analyzes return patterns across pincodes/products/customers'); Settlement Insights ('Sends daily settlement summary via WhatsApp'). Source type: Razorpay-marketing (but the extracted fact is product inventory, not a performance claim, so the launch-publicity rule is not engaged). Razorpay newsroom (12 Mar 2026) names Nugget by Zomato and SuperU as BUILD PARTNERS for Abandoned Cart, and ElevenLabs as voice partner for Subscription Recovery; The Tribune (press, 12 Mar 2026) calls SuperU the 'first external agent on the Agent Studio'. CRITICAL CORRECTION: the newsroom release and all press coverage name only four agents as production-ready at launch — Abandoned Cart Conversion, Dispute Responder, Subscription Recovery, Cashflow Forecaster. RTO Shield, RTO Insights and Settlement Insights appear as cards but are NOT in the production-ready list. Early-access status confirmed: the page carries a 'Get Early Access' CTA and labels the No-Code Agent Builder '(beta)'. | business_impact: NO MAGNITUDE FOUND — no adoption, agent-run volume or outcome numbers published. | who_suffers: merchants (uncovered workflows), Razorpay (product gap). | current_razorpay_solution: Agent Studio — Dispute Responder, Subscription Recovery, Abandoned Cart Conversion (SuperU / Nugget), Cashflow Forecaster, RTO Shield, RTO Insights, Settlement Insights. | remaining_gap: none of the eight cards addresses fund holds/account freezes, refund failures, B2B receivables/collections, GST/TDS line matching, or reconciliation exception resolution. IMPORTANT: the two claims asserting this coverage gap as read off the page FAILED verification 0-3, and the live Aug 2026 roster could NOT be confirmed (razorpay.com/agent-studio/ is client-side rendered and returned navigation chrome with zero agent cards), so 'Agent Studio has exactly seven agents as of Aug 2026' is UNVERIFIED — the March launch page is a historical artefact and Razorpay states the studio 'will evolve into an open ecosystem' with third-party publishers. | verdict: PARTIALLY SOLVED for the four production-ready domains; OPEN for the uncovered ones.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED — Phase-1 finding #6 survives: Razorpay's Vulcan performance figures are self-reported beta results with no published methodology, baseline or sample period, and Razorpay did not supply them when a journalist asked directly. No independent audit, third-party case study with numbers, or Razorpay engineering post carrying a baseline was located.
findings.evidence: problem: Vulcan's headline uplift numbers are being used as evidence of solved problems when they are unverifiable vendor self-report. | evidence: MediaNama, 'Razorpay launches Vulcan, an AI foundation model for payments. But what does it train on?', 18 Aug 2026 (six days before the analysis date; verified via text-extraction proxy as medianama.com 403s direct fetch). Verbatim: 'These are Razorpay's own beta results. It has not published the methodology, baseline or sample period behind them.' The article enumerates exactly the disputed metrics as Razorpay-reported beta figures: '8-10% improvement in payment success rates', '8x more international card fraud detected', '5x more fraudulent or disputed transactions identified', and a 40% increase in shoppers shown their preferred UPI app yielding ~1-2 lakh additional purchases monthly. MediaNama states it sent Razorpay written questions specifically asking it to disclose 'the baseline, sample size, and timeframe' and closes 'This article will be updated on a response' — i.e. affirmative reporting of an absence, not analyst inference. Source type: press (independent Indian tech-policy outlet, adversarial framing — not press-release reprinting). Verifier attempted to locate a Razorpay-authored methodology post: razorpay.com/blog/razorpay-vulcan-ai-model/ returns 404. | business_impact: the five Vulcan numbers themselves are NOT usable as magnitudes — treat as marketing. | who_suffers: analysts and merchants relying on the claims; not a merchant-facing problem per se. | current_razorpay_solution: Vulcan (AI foundation model for payments). | remaining_gap: no baseline, no sample period, no sample size, no third-party audit; status is dated 18 Aug 2026 and could change if Razorpay answered MediaNama afterwards. | verdict: OPEN (as an evidence gap). Preferred wording is 'self-reported beta results with undisclosed methodology' rather than the pejorative 'unaudited vendor marketing', which is the analyst's characterisation, not MediaNama's.

findings.claim: JOB 2 PARTIAL FILL — There is no India-specific or mobile-vs-desktop cart-abandonment benchmark in Baymard's 50-study dataset, so every India abandonment figure used to size Magic Checkout is either vendor-network data with no published methodology or an unverified transfer of a US/EU benchmark. The only defensible citable number is Baymard's global 70.22% average.
findings.evidence: problem: checkout abandonment in Indian e-commerce cannot currently be sized from an independent, methodology-published source. | evidence: Baymard Institute list (last updated 22 Sep 2025; checked 24 Aug 2026), '70.22% - average documented online shopping cart abandonment rate'. Source type: industry-report. A verifier enumerated all 50 entries (Uptain 2025 71.72%, SaleCycle 2023 79.53%, Fresh Relevance 2022 68.70%, Kibo 2021 79.30%, Barilliance 2019 77.13%, Adobe 2016 75.50%, IBM/Coremetrics 2007-2015, Forrester 2009/2010, Comscore 2012, MarketingSherpa 2006, etc.) — every study is a single global/undifferentiated figure with no country or device tag; ZERO India-specific studies; ZERO mobile-vs-desktop split. Baymard's own scope note states its research covers 'leading ecommerce sites in US and Europe', and its 344-site UX benchmark contains no Indian sites. The widely circulated 80.45% mobile / 68.62% desktop split traces to Dynamic Yield's customer network, NOT Baymard. India figures that DO exist are all lower-grade: GoKwik blog 73.12% across Indian D2C (Feb 2026, vendor network data, no published methodology); Razorpay Learn/blog claiming India mobile cart abandonment ~85% and 'below 65% is a strong benchmark for Indian D2C' (razorpay.com/learn/cart-abandonment-rate-101/, razorpay.com/blog/mobile-checkout-india-reduce-load-failures/ — Razorpay-marketing, unsourced, self-interested). | business_impact: 70.22% global average abandonment (Baymard, 22 Sep 2025); India-specific: NO CREDIBLE MAGNITUDE FOUND. | who_suffers: merchants (lost conversion), Razorpay (unsizable TAM for Magic Checkout). | current_razorpay_solution: Magic Checkout; Abandoned Cart Conversion agent (partner-built). | remaining_gap: Razorpay's Magic Checkout uplift figures (22% abandonment reduction; Reload Casuals 27.37%->43.22%; Root Deep +30%; Ecentric +40%) are co-marketing case studies with no baseline or methodology and must NOT be treated as measured results. CAVEAT: Baymard's 70.22% is itself a meta-average of vendor-published studies (SaleCycle, Barilliance, Listrak, Kibo are all abandoned-cart-recovery vendors), i.e. secondary aggregation of self-interested data, not gold-standard primary research; and 'no India benchmark exists' is a universal negative tested by several searches, not exhaustively. The separate claim decomposing abandonment CAUSES (extra costs 40%, delivery too slow 20%, etc., implying only ~35% is addressable by a one-click checkout) FAILED verification 0-3 and must not be used. | verdict: OPEN — problem is real but unsized for India.

findings.claim: JOB 2 PARTIAL FILL / MISUSE WARNING — India's headline 7.1% suspected-digital-fraud rate (2025, nearly double the 3.8% global rate) is an economy-wide figure dominated by high-rate sectors like logistics (16.3%) and telecom (14.7%) and must NOT be used as an e-commerce or payment-gateway fraud rate; the sectors a payment aggregator actually serves sit at or below the global average.
findings.vote: 3-0 (unanimous, but vendor-primary industry report; the sector-level sub-claims separately failed 0-3 and 1-2)
findings.evidence: problem: no valid India-specific merchant-side payment fraud rate is available, and the widely quoted 7.1% figure would overstate Razorpay-relevant exposure by roughly 3x to 6x. | evidence: TransUnion H1 2026 Top Fraud Trends Report, published 16 Jun 2026, via its own India newsroom (vendor-primary) and Business Standard (press, 16 Jun 2026): 'In 2025, 7.1% of attempted transactions involving consumers in India were suspected to be digital fraud, almost double the global rate' of 3.8% (7.1/3.8 = 1.87x). Sector breakdown for India 2025: Logistics 16.3%, Telecom 14.7%, Insurance 11.5%, Gaming 9.6%, Communities 4.7%, Financial services 2.6%, Retail 2.5%, Travel & leisure 0.5%. Attack-stage split for India: login 3.9%, account creation 3.1%, financial transactions 1.2%. Telecom showed +308% YoY rise in suspected fraud attempts 2024->2025. No published methodological criticism or contradicting source was located; figures reproduce identically across TransUnion's newsroom, Business Standard (two pieces), Outlook Business, Deccan Chronicle, Analytics Insight and NewsGram. | business_impact: economy-wide 7.1% of attempted transactions suspected fraud (India, CY2025); retail 2.5%; financial services 2.6%; financial-transaction stage 1.2%. NOTE THE VOTING INCONSISTENCY: this parent claim passed 3-0 with the sector numbers cited in its own verification evidence, yet the standalone claims stating retail 2.5% / FS 2.6% and the attack-stage split failed 0-3 and 1-2 respectively. The sector and stage figures should therefore be treated as MEDIUM-LOW confidence, usable only with that flag. | who_suffers: merchants and end customers; Razorpay indirectly. | current_razorpay_solution: Razorpay Thirdwatch / RTO Shield / Vulcan fraud detection (none independently benchmarked). | remaining_gap: 'suspected' fraud includes transactions denied for corporate policy violations, not just confirmed fraud, so the metric is inflated; the sample is TransUnion/TruValidate customers' assessed transactions, not a census of Indian digital commerce; there is still NO India merchant-side chargeback rate and NO India dispute-rate benchmark of any kind. | verdict: OPEN — magnitude for the RISK domain remains genuinely unavailable; the honest cell is 'no valid proxy found'.

findings.claim: NEGATIVE FINDING (absence of evidence, reported as required) — Five of eight Phase-1 findings and six of seven JOB-2 magnitudes produced NO claim that survived adversarial verification, and none of the six prioritised Razorpay source types except the Agent Studio launch blog yielded surviving evidence. These cells must be carried forward as UNVERIFIED, not as established.
findings.vote: n/a — derived from the verification round's own failure record (16 claims voted down)
findings.evidence: problem: the evidence base is far thinner than the Phase-1 finding list implies. | evidence (what FAILED): Phase-1 #1 (>20M monthly UPI AutoPay revocations for insufficient balance; SBI ~30% approval / ~70% failure) — three supporting claims voted 0-3 and one 1-2; the Business Standard URL 403s to direct fetch and its text was recovered only via search-index extraction, so the wording is near-verbatim at best. Phase-1 #2 (92-96% blended UPI success, ~0.7-0.8% technical decline, residual failure is business decline) — the only supporting claim, on mandate failure being business decline, failed 0-3; no NPCI or merchant-observed success-rate evidence survived. Phase-1 #4 (fund holds/freezes with named triggers and resolution bands) — the two supporting claims failed 0-3, and the regulator-grounded KYC-cliff claim (merchants onboarded to 31 Dec 2025 to be compliant within a year; from 1 Jan 2026 due diligence at onboarding with CKYCR retrieval) also failed 0-3. Phase-1 #5 (refunds as the single most frequent complaint category) — no supporting claim survived; the two RBI Ombudsman claims failed 0-3, and they in fact point the other way (Loans & Advances 29.25% and Credit Cards 20.04% lead FY25 complaints; Mobile/Electronic Banking complaints DOWN 12.74% YoY; ATM/Debit Card down to 7.47% from 14.56% in FY23). Phase-1 #7 (DRHP confidentially pre-filed ~12 Jun 2026, not public) — NOT TESTED; no claim, surviving or refuted, addressed it, so no company-authored Risk Factors section was obtained. JOB-2 magnitudes with NO surviving number: RTO rate and cost per RTO (three Unicommerce-sourced claims — COD RTO 58% vs prepaid <15%, blended festive peak 39.2%, a 39%->21% reduction case — ALL failed 0-3); refund failure/delay rate (nothing found at all); SME DSO / MSME Samadhaan / TReDS receivables (nothing found at all); reconciliation hours or FTEs (nothing found at all); subscription involuntary churn from failed mandates (nothing found; the supporting e-mandate volume denominator, ~1.6bn transactions at top-ten remitter banks in May 2026 vs 577m in May 2025, failed 0-3 twice). SOURCE TYPES NOT REACHED: (a) Razorpay engineering blog — nothing; (b) Razorpay research reports incl. 'The Era of Rising Bharat' — nothing; (c) 2026 leadership interviews (Harshil Mathur, Shashank Kumar, AI/product leads) — nothing; (d) RazorpayX / business banking — nothing; (e) Razorpay developer documentation — the one docs-based claim (settlements T+2, and Instant Settlements requiring a manual support ticket) failed 0-3 and 1-2; (f) 2026 newsroom — only the Agent Studio release. DOMAINS WITH NO CREDIBLE EVIDENCE OF A RAZORPAY-RELEVANT PROBLEM AFTER VERIFICATION: REVENUE (failed-payment recovery, collections, overdue receivables, revenue leakage); FINANCE (reconciliation, settlement mismatches, invoice matching, GST/TDS matching, exception handling); GROWTH (agentic commerce, AI-readable catalogs, upsell, conversational commerce); OPERATIONS (merchant onboarding, integration friction, support, troubleshooting). PAYMENTS and RISK have only the two partial magnitudes above. | business_impact: NO MAGNITUDE FOUND for all of the above. | who_suffers: unknown/unquantified. | current_razorpay_solution: n/a. | remaining_gap: the entire JOB-2 magnitude table is effectively empty. | verdict: OPEN — honest empty cells, per the instruction to prefer these over plausible invention.

caveats: 1) VOTE MECHANICS: a 0-3 vote means verifiers did not confirm the claim, which is NOT the same as the underlying fact being false. Several down-voted claims (20M UPI AutoPay revocations, SBI ~30% approval, Unicommerce RTO rates, e-mandate volume) may well be true but currently lack verified sourcing — they should be re-researched, not asserted and not discarded as disproven. 2) INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IN THE VOTING: the TransUnion parent claim passed 3-0 while its own sector breakdown (retail 2.5%, FS 2.6%) and attack-stage split (transaction stage 1.2%) failed as standalone claims, even though those figures appear inside the passing claim's verification evidence. Treat the sector/stage numbers as medium-low and re-verify before citing. 3) FETCH FAILURES DISTORTED COVERAGE: business-standard.com and medianama.com both 403 direct fetch (recovered via search-index/text-proxy extraction — treat quotes as near-verbatim); razorpay.com/agent-studio/ is client-side rendered and returned zero agent cards, so the LIVE Aug 2026 Agent Studio roster is unconfirmed; razorpay.com/blog/razorpay-vulcan-ai-model/ returns 404. 4) SEARCH BUDGET EXHAUSTED on the Vulcan thread (200/200 queries), so the negative — that no independent audit or baseline exists — is a non-exhaustive negative. 5) TIME SENSITIVITY: the MediaNama Vulcan piece is explicitly a living article pending Razorpay's reply and is only 6 days old, so the 'no methodology published' status must be dated 18 Aug 2026, not stated as permanent; the Agent Studio blog is 5 months old (12 Mar 2026) and Razorpay says the studio will become an open ecosystem, so the roster may have grown. 6) SCOPE LIMIT ON THE T+1 REFUTATION: only the RBI PA Master Direction was examined; NPCI/card-scheme rules, nodal-account rules, and Razorpay's actual merchant agreement were not, and the 2025 MD does retain a fairness-and-transparency obligation, so a weaker disclosure argument survives. 7) BENCHMARK QUALITY: Baymard's 70.22% is a meta-average of studies published by abandoned-cart-recovery vendors, not primary research, so calling it a 'gold standard' overstates it; and TransUnion 'suspected fraud' includes policy-violation denials, not confirmed loss. 8) THE CRITICAL RULE BIT HARD: after excluding Razorpay's own launch publicity as results, essentially nothing quantitative about Razorpay's product performance remains — Magic Checkout uplift, Vulcan metrics, and Agent Studio efficacy are all vendor self-report with no baseline. 9) Phase-1 finding #7 (DRHP confidential) was never tested by any claim in this round; its status is unknown, not confirmed.
